data.name: Khilaaf
data.gender_notes: Khilaaf is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who rules or rebels against an established authority. The name Khilaaf carries the meaning “Ruler, Rebel” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Khilaaf usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler, rebel and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder to seek wisdom and understanding before making decisions that challenge the status quo
data.etymology: Khilaaf belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ruler, Rebel.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khilaaf total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: خلاف
in_arabic.long_meaning: الخلاف يأتي من الجذر الخ ل ف، ويراد به المقابل أو المعاكس، ويكون الخلاف بين الفرد أو الجانب أو الموقف، والخلاف له عدة مقالات في الإسلام مثل الإختلافات في الفقه والآراء في العقيدة والمنازعات الحكومية، ويتسم الخلاف بالعدوانية والمبارحة وعدم التوصل إلى حل سلمي، ويجب على المسلمين الاهتمام بحل الخلافات السلميًا وعدم القتال والعدوان، وقد ورد الخلاف في القرآن الكريم في آيات كثيرة مثل (وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَا زَاغَ الظَنُّ فِي الْقُلُوبِ وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ يُزَيهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيُضِلُّ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيُسبِحُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَا يَشاءُ الْعَلِيُّ الرَ‌حِيمُ)

in_urdu.name: خلاف
in_urdu.long_meaning: خلاف کا مطلب ہے مخالف، منازع اور مقابل، اسلام میں خلاف کو مختلف موضوعات پر بہت سے حوالے مل جاتے ہیں جیسے فقه میں اختلاف، عقیدے میں اختلافات اور حکومت میں منازعات، خلاف کا مطلب ہے عدوانیت، مباحثہ اور سلمی حل کے بغیر، مسلموں پر ہے کہ وہ سلمی حل سے خلافات کو حل کریں اور جنگ اور عدوان کے بجائے سلمی حل کی کوشش کریں، قرآن کریم میں خلاف کے بارے میں بہت سے آیات موجود ہیں جیسے (وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَا زَاغَ الظَنُّ فِي الْقُلُوبِ وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ يُزَيهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيُضِلُّ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيُسبِحُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَا يَشاءُ الْعَلِيُّ الرَ‌حِيمُ)

in_hindi.name: खिलाफ
in_hindi.long_meaning: खिलाफ का अर्थ है विरोधी, विरोधी और विपरीत, इस्लाम में खिलाफ को कई विषयों पर बहुत से उल्लेख मिलते हैं जैसे कि फ़सह में विविधता, विश्वास में विवाद और सरकार में, खिलाफ का अर्थ है आक्रामकता, बहस और शांतिपूर्ण समाधान के बिना, मुसलमानों पर है कि वे शांतिपूर्ण समाधान से खिलाफों को हल करें और युद्ध और आक्रामकता के बजाय शांतिपूर्ण समाधान का प्रयास करें, क़ुरआन में खिलाफ के बारे में कई आयात हैं जैसे (वलो शाओ लाहू मा जाग ना ज़ुन फ़ी अल-क़ुलुबी वलकिन्न लाहू युजना इया शाएौ वयुयल्लाहू युजना इया शाएौ वयुसबिहू लाहू अलै मा यशाओ अल-आली अर-रहीम)

in_english.name: Khilaaf
in_english.long_meaning: Khilaaf originates from the Arabic root kh-l-f, meaning opposite or contradictory, and can refer to differences in opinion or action, Khilaaf is often associated with hostility, debate, and conflict, however Muslims are encouraged to resolve disputes peacefully, without resorting to violence or aggression, the Quran mentions Khilaaf in several verses, such as (And if Allah had willed, He would have guided them to a straight path, but He rejects those who refuse to believe and He leads astray those who are wicked, and He is exalted in might, wise)

data.cultural_impact: The term "Khilaaf" originated from the Arabic word "khalifa," which means "representative" or "successor." Historically, it refers to the political leader or caliph, who ruled the Islamic world following the Prophet Muhammad's death. The term holds great significance in Islamic history as it represented the political authority of the Muslim community. The caliphate system established by the Rashidun, Umayyad, Abbasid, and Ottoman empires significantly impacted the Islamic world by promoting a unified political unity, establishing a centralized administration, and spreading the message of Islam through military conquests and diplomacy.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the term "Khilaaf" also symbolizes the rebellion or resistance against the established spiritual authorities, reflecting the Islamic concept of "khilafat-i-Rasoolillah," or the Caliphate of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The Prophet Muhammad was the ultimate spiritual and political leader for the Muslim community. The term "Khilaaf" reminds us of the importance of remaining committed to our spiritual ideals and resisting any temptations towards deviation, staying true to our faith. Thus, the term "Khilaaf" holds a profound spiritual significance, as it encourages us to remain steadfast in our commitment to our faith, resisting any opposing forces that try to lead us astray.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Ruler, Rebel" symbolizes One who rules or rebels against an established authority. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Khilaaf serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of ruler, rebel.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture
